candidates: Orbital abscess secondary to acute dacryocystitis
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI
champion: Orbital abscess secondary to acute dacryocystitis

raw.champion: Orbital abscess secondary to acute dacryocystitis
raw.rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast, along with postseptal fat stranding and increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT, supports this diagnosis. The patient's history of epiphora and the isolation of Streptococcus pyogenes also point towards an infectious process originating from the lacrimal sac.

rejected.label: Acute Dacryocystitis with Orbital Cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of epiphora and the imaging shows opacification of both nasolacrimal ducts, the primary issue appears to be the formation of an abscess, which is a more severe complication than cellulitis alone.

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis secondary to dacryocystitis
rejected.why: The presence of an abscess, as indicated by imaging studies, suggests a more localized and severe infection than cellulitis, which is typically characterized by diffuse inflammation.
